 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Ms. Deliah Bernard, former Senior Indigenous Affairs Advisor in the Office of the Prime Minister, has been granted a reduction of her limitation period under section 36 to permit her to accept a contract with the Assembly of First Nations (AFN). 
Ms. Bernard applied for a reduction of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The reduction allows Ms. Bernard to accept a contract with AFN. 
In reviewing Ms. Bernard’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following: 
The general employment prospects of the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder:
- Ms. Bernard is specialized on the subject matter and offers unique experience in issues of great relevance to all parties involved.
The nature and significance to the Government of Canada of the information possessed by the former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office:
- The contract with the AFN does not overlap with the responsibilities she held in her previous role as a reporting public office holder.
The degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage by hiring the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder:
- Ms. Bernard will not be expected to negotiate nor make representations to federal government on behalf of the AFN. There is no competition nor commercial advantage to be gained by hiring Ms. Bernard. Her role will be to provide advice on prioritizing and ranking issues of discussion with the premiers, with the objective of strengthening relationships between First Nations and provincial and territorial governments.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the reduction in relation to Ms. Bernard’s contract with the AFN outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period. 
All other post‐employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Ms. Bernard’s limitation period.
